questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have teaching in exotic animals.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a really good experience and you meet really interesting people. But a lot of the consultations was in dutch, which of course made it harder to participate fully in the consultation. The students was very helpful to translate.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took some time, some of the informations was not that easy to find, and also there was a lot of them! For future students, please read everything again, to make sure you don't miss interesting opportunities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mentors from the university, and we had a welcome event at the campus. Also we could always send an email and ask questions, so in general the assistance was great!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The first days was confusing, but people were very friendly and helpful to answer questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that I found a room. I found it through Facebook, but I also met people who lived in Airbnb and hotels because it was impossible to find anything. I would recommend people to start searching for a place early, and be very aware of scammers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved to live off campus! I lived in the middle between the campus and the city center. The campus for veterinary medicine is quite far away from the city, and also from the dorms (which is in the city center). The options for public transportation in Ghent is quite bad, and the city center is the place to go for an evening out etc., and then it is nice that you don't have to bike 10 km everytime :-)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot exchange students in Ghent compared to the university dorms. On the other hand is the university dorms far away from campus Merelbeke. The private market can be quite expensive unless you are lucky.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy, there was very good guidelines.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register on a website from the university, and we also had to send proof of tetanus vaccination etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always contact the contactpeson of the faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though it is a clinical traineeship, you can also sign up for other classes at Ugent! If you for example want to learn the language etc. and the classes is in the evening!. So be aware of that opportunity, as they don't really tell you about that option.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a traineeship, and the level was last year student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit different. They had more cases, but we had to follow the vet and watch a lot, they did not have time to ask you everything and let you present a plan, differentialdiagnoses etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical traineeship in small animals and
Lower country studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As it is a clinical traineeship where you don't choose your clinics yourself, I can't recommend anything. I can recommend to check for other courses in Ugent if you have interest in any other kind of lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not anything as I remember

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Restaurants and bars is quite cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know there is a lot of options, but I never used them :-)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different sport, swimming etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel! Belgium is a small country and you can quickly cross the borders to the netherlands, france, luxemburg and germany

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wallonia is a very beutiful part of Belgium. Close to Ghent is Bruges, which is a really beautiful city. France is nearby, and it is easy to go there with flixbus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the culture is very close to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be very social actives the first weeks, meet people with an open mind! It was more easy to make a lot of contacts the first weeks, before people split into groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of normal coffee places, because everyone goes to bars instead in Belgium.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people in Belgium goes out a lot, and everyday the bars is filled, and there is different activities, concert etc. There is always an event going on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Search accommodation early
2. Beware of scammers when you are searching accommodation
3. Be openminded and participate in the events for international students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rent a bike! It is the easiest way to come around the city, and there is no public transportation in the night.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: You find really good friends, and to do a lot of travelling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language. Because it is not lecture, they will speak a lot in dutch, and if the other students does not want to speak english the day can be really long. But most of the people is very nice!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go for it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
